parsed.explanation: No trans-specific presentation offence, facility ban or entry rule is documented, but a same-sex conduct ban upheld in 2024, documented attacks on cross-dressing people, a fraud charge for 'pretending to be a woman', stigma/invisibility, and no SOGI anti-discrimination protection or LGBT support leave an outed visitor with thin recourse. Poverty of trans-specific enforcement, facilities, custody and care evidence is not safety; extrapolating from the active criminal regime and hostile social climate places this at elevated, not high, risk.

entry_documents.interaction: No visa/entry-screening rule is sourced; a relationship read as same-sex would not be recognised, but that is not a documented border practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: In 2019 a cross-dressing teenager was assaulted then charged with fraud for allegedly pretending to be a woman; charge withdrawn in May 2019. Custody placement is not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Withdrawal of the 2019 charge shows a limited remedy in that case, not a general protection.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch or presentation could, on this precedent, become a fraud investigation rather than a documented custody rule.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No facilities law or practice is sourced; do not infer a ban or access from the same-sex conduct provisions.

care_services.interaction: Sources name only a regional HIV organisation as a contact point for MSM; no healthcare, medication or emergency-care evidence for trans visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Sections 146/148 criminalise consensual sex between men, up to 10/5 years, upheld by the High Court on 16 Feb 2024. As a secondary factor, stigma and the 2019 'pretending' fraud charge show a possible police lever against gender nonconformity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No SOGI anti-discrimination law; no documented trans-specific offence and no enforcement frequency data.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The sexuality statute does not by itself prove routine trans targeting, but combined with stigma, no recourse and the fraud precedent it raises severity if outed.

minors_guardians.exposure: No visitor/minor travel rule is documented. A resident cross-dressing teenager was assaulted and fraud-charged in 2019.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented; no LGBT youth helpline or help centre exists.
minors_guardians.interaction: For a travelling minor the operative risk is the same undocumented facilities, police and care exposure as for an adult, with no documented guardian-specific safeguard.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Three cross-dressing young men were physically attacked in Sept 2018; a 2023 58-page report documents LGBT bias-motivated violence and discrimination in daily life, without trans-specific denominators.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The head of government condemned the 2018 attacks as unacceptable homophobia; no prosecution or victim remedy is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Official condemnation is a weak positive, but dated incidents plus no legal protection leave street hostility largely unremedied.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI anti-discrimination or harassment law, no dedicated LGBT organisation, thin/invisible social infrastructure, and the 2024 court ruling closed the constitutional route.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented beyond condemnation and one withdrawn charge.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns on entry, facilities, custody, screening and care cannot be treated as safety; they widen uncertainty around an already hostile climate.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower risk than 0.35-C: no documented routine police stops, extortion or overnight detention of trans visitors, and the one fraud charge was withdrawn. Higher risk than a merely disapproving setting because attacks, stigma and an actively upheld criminal ban coincide.

Similar-to-below 0.55-C: both have a same-sex offence and recurring hostility, but 0.55-C has familiar gender-diverse roles and a documented assault prosecution, whereas this dossier shows stigma, no roles, no SOGI law and no documented prosecution.

Materially below 0.75-C: there the old statute is a documented dead letter, a gender-diverse role is respected and a court awarded enforced compensation. Here the ban was upheld in 2024, society is stigmatised, and no equivalent remedy is documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no documented universal traveller-facing ban, but an outed visitor meets an actively upheld same-sex criminal framework, documented violence against cross-dressing people, a fraud-as-pretending precedent, and no SOGI recourse or support infrastructure. Facilities, custody, entry and care are undocumented, so uncertainty is extrapolated downward from criminalisation, stigma and absence of relief rather than toward neutrality. That interaction—moderate, dated street/police exposure amplified by no remedy—fits elevated risk.
